passages.text: Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the churches of Macedonia.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul wants them to know something important.
God gave grace to the churches in Macedonia.
Paul wants the Corinthians to know about this grace.
passages.original: Γνωρίζομεν δὲ ὑμῖν ἀδελφοί τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν δεδομένην ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Μακεδονίας

passages.text: In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.
passages.sermon:
The churches of Macedonia suffered a terrible ordeal.
They had abundant joy.
They also had deep poverty.
Their joy and poverty overflowed.
This overflow became rich generosity.
passages.original: ὅτι ἐν πολλῇ δοκιμῇ θλίψεως ἡ περισσεία τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία αὐτῶν ἐπερίσσευσεν εἰς τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς ἁπλότητος αὐτῶν

passages.text: For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord, they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.
passages.sermon:
The churches of Macedonia gave generously.
They gave as much as they were able.
They even gave more than they could afford.
They chose to give freely.
They begged us to let them help.
They wanted to share in serving the saints.
passages.original: ὅτι κατὰ δύναμιν μαρτυρῶ καὶ παρὰ δύναμιν αὐθαίρετοι μετὰ πολλῆς παρακλήσεως δεόμενοι ἡμῶν τὴν χάριν καὶ τὴν κοινωνίαν τῆς διακονίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους

passages.text: And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, because it was the will of God.
passages.sermon:
The Macedonian believers acted in a surprising way.
They did not only do what we expected.
They gave themselves first to the Lord.
They also gave themselves to us.
They did this because God wanted it.
passages.original: καὶ οὐ καθὼς ἠλπίσαμεν ἀλλ’ ἑαυτοὺς ἔδωκαν πρῶτον τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ ἡμῖν διὰ θελήματος Θεοῦ

passages.text: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Corinthians.
Paul and his companions wanted the Corinthians to finish their act of giving.
Titus was a fellow worker with Paul.
Paul and his companions urged Titus to visit the Corinthians.
Titus had already started helping the Corinthians with this act of grace.
Paul and his companions asked Titus to help the Corinthians finish this act of grace.
passages.original: Εἰς τὸ παρακαλέσαι ἡμᾶς Τίτον ἵνα καθὼς προενήρξατο οὕτως καὶ ἐπιτελέσῃ εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ τὴν χάριν ταύτην

passages.text: But just as you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you —see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthian Christians.
You excel in many things.
You excel in faith.
You excel in speech.
You excel in knowledge.
You excel in complete earnestness.
You excel in the love that we inspired in you.
Now, make sure you also excel in this grace of giving.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ὥσπερ ἐν παντὶ περισσεύετε πίστει καὶ λόγῳ καὶ γνώσει καὶ πάσῃ σπουδῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν ἀγάπῃ ἵνα καὶ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ χάριτι περισσεύητε

passages.text: I am not making a demand, but I am testing the sincerity of your love in comparison to the earnestness of others.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthian church.
Paul does not command them to give.
Paul does not make a demand.
Paul compares their love to the earnestness of others.
Paul tests if their love is sincere.
Paul uses the zeal of others as a standard.
Paul wants to see if their love is genuine.
passages.original: Οὐ κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν λέγω ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς ἑτέρων σπουδῆς καὶ τὸ τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀγάπης γνήσιον δοκιμάζων

passages.text: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.
passages.sermon:
Our Lord Jesus Christ is full of grace.
Jesus was rich.
Jesus became poor for your sake.
He did this so that you could become rich through His poverty.
passages.original: Γινώσκετε γὰρ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὅτι δι’ ὑμᾶς ἐπτώχευσεν πλούσιος ὤν ἵνα ὑμεῖς τῇ ἐκείνου πτωχείᾳ πλουτήσητε

passages.text: And this is my opinion about what is helpful for you in this matter: Last year you were the first not only to give, but even to have such a desire.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthian Christians.
Paul gives his opinion about what is helpful for them.
Paul says this advice will benefit them.
Last year, these Christians were the first to want to give.
They were also the first to actually begin giving.
passages.original: καὶ γνώμην ἐν τούτῳ δίδωμι τοῦτο γὰρ ὑμῖν συμφέρει οἵτινες οὐ μόνον τὸ ποιῆσαι ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ θέλειν προενήρξασθε ἀπὸ πέρυσι

passages.text: Now finish the work, so that you may complete it just as eagerly as you began, according to your means.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christians in Corinth.
He urges them to finish the work they started.
They began this work with eagerness.
Paul tells them to complete the work with the same eagerness.
He instructs them to give according to what they have.
passages.original: νυνὶ δὲ καὶ τὸ ποιῆσαι ἐπιτελέσατε ὅπως καθάπερ ἡ προθυμία τοῦ θέλειν οὕτως καὶ τὸ ἐπιτελέσαι ἐκ τοῦ ἔχειν

passages.text: For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians about giving.
Paul says eagerness matters.
If a person is eager to give, God accepts the gift.
God accepts the gift based on what the person has.
God does not expect a gift based on what the person does not have.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ἡ προθυμία πρόκειται καθὸ ἐὰν ἔχῃ εὐπρόσδεκτος οὐ καθὸ οὐκ ἔχει

passages.text: It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthian Christians.
Paul explains his intention about giving.
Paul does not want others to have relief while the Corinthians suffer.
Paul wants equality among believers.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ ἵνα ἄλλοις ἄνεσις ὑμῖν θλῖψις ἀλλ’ ἐξ ἰσότητος

passages.text: At the present time, your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need. Then there will be equality.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians.
He speaks about giving and sharing.
Right now, you have more than you need.
Others do not have enough.
You can help them with your extra.
Later, they may have more than they need.
Then, they can help you if you are in need.
This way, everyone will have enough.
This brings equality.
passages.original: ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ τὸ ὑμῶν περίσσευμα εἰς τὸ ἐκείνων ὑστέρημα ἵνα καὶ τὸ ἐκείνων περίσσευμα γένηται εἰς τὸ ὑμῶν ὑστέρημα ὅπως γένηται ἰσότης

passages.text: As it is written: “He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.”
passages.sermon: Scripture says this.\r\nThe person who gathered much did not have extra.\r\nThe person who gathered little did not lack anything.
passages.original: καθὼς γέγραπται Ὁ τὸ πολὺ οὐκ ἐπλεόνασεν καὶ ὁ τὸ ὀλίγον οὐκ ἠλαττόνησεν

passages.text: But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you.
passages.sermon:
God deserves thanks.
God gave Titus a special devotion.
This devotion is for you.
God put this same devotion in Titus’s heart.
I also have this devotion for you.
passages.original: Χάρις δὲ τῷ Θεῷ τῷ διδόντι τὴν αὐτὴν σπουδὴν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ Τίτου

passages.text: For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.
passages.sermon:
Titus is coming to you.
He is coming eagerly.
He is coming by his own choice.
He welcomed our appeal.
passages.original: ὅτι τὴν μὲν παράκλησιν ἐδέξατο σπουδαιότερος δὲ ὑπάρχων αὐθαίρετος ἐξῆλθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthians.
Paul and his companions are sending Titus to the Corinthians.
They are also sending another brother with Titus.
All the churches praise this brother.
The churches praise him for his work in the gospel.
Paul and his companions send this brother along with Titus.
passages.original: Συνεπέμψαμεν δὲ μετ’ αὐτοῦ τὸν ἀδελφὸν οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διὰ πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν

passages.text: More than that, this brother was chosen by the churches to accompany us with the offering —the gracious gift we administer to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help.
passages.sermon:
This brother was chosen by the churches.
He will travel with us.
He will help us deliver the offering.
We administer this offering as a gracious gift.
We do this to honor the Lord Himself.
We also do this to show our eagerness to help.
passages.original: οὐ μόνον δὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ χειροτονηθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν συνέκδημος ἡμῶν σὺν τῇ χάριτι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφ’ ἡμῶν πρὸς τὴν αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου δόξαν καὶ προθυμίαν ἡμῶν

passages.text: We hope to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.
passages.sermon:
We want to avoid criticism.
We are giving this generous gift.
We are the ones administering it.
We act carefully so no one can blame us.
passages.original: στελλόμενοι τοῦτο μή τις ἡμᾶς μωμήσηται ἐν τῇ ἁδρότητι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφ’ ἡμῶν

passages.text: For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.
passages.sermon: We take great care to do what is right.\r\nWe do what is right before the Lord.\r\nWe also do what is right before people.
passages.original: προνοοῦμεν γὰρ καλὰ οὐ μόνον ἐνώπιον Κυρίου ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐνώπιον ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: And we are sending along with them our brother whose earnestness has been proven many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you.
passages.sermon:
We are sending our brother with them.
We have tested this brother many times.
He has shown great earnestness in many situations.
Now he is even more earnest.
He has great confidence in you.
passages.original: Συνεπέμψαμεν δὲ αὐτοῖς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν ὃν ἐδοκιμάσαμεν ἐν πολλοῖς πολλάκις σπουδαῖον ὄντα νυνὶ δὲ πολὺ σπουδαιότερον πεποιθήσει πολλῇ τῇ εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, to the glory of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Titus is my partner.
Titus works together with you.
Our brothers are messengers from the churches.
These brothers bring glory to Christ.
passages.original: εἴτε ὑπὲρ Τίτου κοινωνὸς ἐμὸς καὶ εἰς ὑμᾶς συνεργός εἴτε ἀδελφοὶ ἡμῶν ἀπόστολοι ἐκκλησιῶν δόξα Χριστοῦ

passages.text: In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you.
passages.sermon:
You are part of the church in Achaia.
Many other churches are watching you.
Some men are coming to you.
Show these men your love.
Let everyone see your love clearly.
Show them why we boast about you.
Let all the churches see the proof of your love and our confidence in you.
passages.original: τὴν οὖν ἔνδειξιν τῆς ἀγάπης ὑμῶν καὶ ἡμῶν καυχήσεως ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν εἰς αὐτοὺς ἐνδεικνύμενοι εἰς πρόσωπον τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν
